findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the pass1.py seam description: the plan claims the current seam is a single `extra` assignment requiring replacement with compositional `extra_parts`, but `pass1.py` lines 420-434 already implement the compositional `context_parts` form for both G5 and `no-file-impact`; either update the plan narrative to reflect the as-found state or identify which part of the seam remains unimplemented.
evidence: Plan states: 'The current pass1.py seam is an inline G5-only branch, not a generic per-criterion dispatcher. Replace the single `extra` assignment with compositional `extra_parts`'

pass1.py lines 427-433 already read: `context_parts: list[str] = []` / `if any(c.get("id") == "G5" ...): context_parts.append(decomp_context)` / `if any(c.get("id") == "no-file-impact" ...): context_parts.append(_no_file_impact_context(ctx))` / `extra = "\n\n".join(context_parts)`
The compositional form described as the TARGET state is already the actual state of the file
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'The current pass1.py seam is an inline G5-only branch, not a generic per-criterion dispatcher. Replace the single `extra` assignment with compositional `extra_parts`' — but pass1.py lines 420-434 already implement the compositional `context_parts` pattern for BOTH G5 and no-file-impact. No single-`extra`-assignment seam exists to replace.
findings.location: Approach / Declared-reason data flow section; pass1.py lines 420-434
scenarios: An implementer reads the plan and believes they must refactor pass1.py, discovers the code already matches the target state, and is confused about whether the plan describes work that is already done or work that was never needed.

If the plan is being reviewed as a spec for new work, a test verifying 'chunk containing both G5 and no-file-impact receives both context blocks' would trivially pass against the existing code — masking whether the plan's implementation guidance was ever followed.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the 'Declared-reason data flow' section to describe what is being ADDED (the `_no_file_impact_context` helper call and the second `context_parts.append(...)` branch), not a wholesale replacement of a single-`extra` seam that no longer exists in the code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the `CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local):` block to `plan_review_no-file-impact.md` listing `assertion_plausible {yes|no|insufficient}`, `reason_grounded {yes|no|insufficient}`, and `repo_file_change_named {yes|no}` with their decision semantics, matching the format used by `necessity`, `asserted_capability`, and `removal_rationale`.
evidence: Plan states: 'The prompt contains a co-located `CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local)` contract defining: `assertion_plausible: yes|no|insufficient`, `reason_grounded: yes|no|insufficient`, `repo_file_change_named: yes|no`'
The committed prompt file (plan_review_no-file-impact.md) has NO `CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local):` section — the file ends at line 36 with only prose decision rules and an ANTI-FP clause.
Analogous criteria all carry this section: plan_review_necessity.md line 49, plan_review_asserted_capability.md line 52, plan_review_removal_rationale.md line 40, plan_review_decomp_shape.md line 60.

The criteria_routing.json `no-file-impact` checklist keys (`assertion_plausible`, `reason_grounded`, `repo_file_change_named`) are routing/guide metadata, not the co-located prompt sub-answer schema the plan specifies.
findings.finding: The prompt file `plan_review_no-file-impact.md` lacks the explicitly required `CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local):` structured block. The plan specifies this section as a co-located contract in the prompt, and all analogous criteria (`necessity`, `asserted_capability`, `removal_rationale`, `decomp_shape`) carry it; but the committed prompt file omits it, leaving the sub-answer schema defined only in prose rather than in the structured format the framework uses for cross-criterion consistency.
findings.location: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no-file-impact.md / Plan section 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery'
scenarios: An LLM executor reading the prompt sees the vocabulary in prose but not in the structured CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS format; downstream structured-output parsing or cross-criterion tooling that expects this section will not find it.
A project overlay author consulting `rebar explain no-file-impact` sees no sub-answer schema to extend, unlike every other criterion with a `criterion-local` section.
findings.suggested_fix:
Append to the prompt file after the ANTI-FP clause:
```
CHECKLIST SUB-ANSWERS (criterion-local):
- assertion_plausible {yes|no|insufficient} — overall verdict on the `none` declaration.
- reason_grounded {yes|no|insufficient} — whether `declared_reason` concretely explains external-only delivery.
- repo_file_change_named {yes|no} — whether the plan names any repository edit (source, tests, config, CI, generated artifact, or documentation).
```

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command for the mutation AC, e.g. a temporary one-line patch to `registry.py` that always returns `True` for `no-file-impact` followed by `pytest <applicability test>` showing failure, then reverting and re-running to show green.
evidence: 'Reintroducing the prior always-selected routing behavior makes at least one held-out applicability test fail, and restoring the implementation makes that test pass.'
'A defect-seeded mutation of the routing predicate must make the held-out applicability test fail.'
No Test Design paragraph describes the mutation step sequence or the proving command to demonstrate the failure/restore cycle.
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion 'Reintroducing the prior always-selected routing behavior makes at least one held-out applicability test fail, and restoring the implementation makes that test pass' has no concrete proving command — no command sequence is described for actually executing the mutation, observing failure, restoring, and observing success.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, second-to-last bullet before operator-attested items; also Test Design, last sentence of held-out oracle paragraph.
scenarios: A reviewer or automated check cannot confirm this property without an explicit mutation procedure; the AC becomes unfalsifiable in CI without a mutation-test harness or manual step documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the mutation step inline in the Test Design: 'To verify mutation sensitivity: temporarily change the `file_impact_scope` predicate in `registry.py` to unconditionally return `True`, run `pytest tests/unit/plan_review/test_registry.py::test_no_file_impact_applicability`, assert failure, revert, assert pass.'

findings.finding: The sub-answer `reason_grounded: yes|no|insufficient` drives three distinct outcomes (PASS, advisory contradiction, non-blocking coaching) but the plan never specifies the evaluative criterion — what makes a `no_file_impact_reason` 'grounded' versus 'not grounded' versus 'insufficient' — alongside the decision rules that consume it. A prompt author receives the field name and its downstream role but no definition of the evaluation protocol for assigning it.
findings.location: Plan section 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' — `reason_grounded` decision rules
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'reason_grounded' evaluation clause to the sub-answer contract block: 'reason_grounded: yes when the declared reason names each deliverable and explains why none requires a repo-file edit; no when the reason is present but makes a claim the plan text contradicts or doesn't support; insufficient when reason is empty, one-word, or too sparse to assess.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the specific test file(s) for each of the six test contracts (applicability, prompt-input, offline rubric, explain, gate, generated-artifact) in the Test Design section, mirroring the precision of the Scope file list.
evidence: 'Focused tests in the existing plan-review, routing, prompt, CLI, and gate test modules selected after the required coverage inventory.'
No file paths are given for any of the six test contracts described in Test Design, unlike the Scope section which names every production file explicitly.
findings.finding: The test design defers the concrete location of new tests to the executor with the phrase 'selected after the required coverage inventory', leaving an executing agent to determine which specific test files receive each of the described test contracts (applicability, prompt-input, offline rubric, explain, gate, generated-artifact).
findings.location: Test Design section, final sentence: '…in the existing plan-review, routing, prompt, CLI, and gate test modules selected after the required coverage inventory.'
scenarios: An executor must perform their own file-discovery step before writing any test, introducing unnecessary ambiguity about whether a new module vs. an existing one should be used.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sub-bullet per test contract naming the target file, e.g. 'Applicability contract → `tests/unit/plan_review/test_registry.py`', 'Prompt-input contract → `tests/unit/plan_review/test_pass1.py`', etc.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fifth offline rubric case in the Test Design for a ticket that reads/analyses repository code without editing it, asserting the criterion returns PASS, to validate the stated 'read-only is compatible' decision rule.
evidence: Approach states: 'Reading or analysing repository code without editing it remains compatible with `none`.'
Test Design lists four cases: (1) external operator action, (2) new CLI flag, (3) docs-only, (4) vague plan — none covers a within-repo read-only analysis scenario.
The rule is part of the criterion's decision logic and would affect what the LLM returns, but no rubric behavior test validates it.
findings.finding: The Approach explicitly states a decision rule — 'Reading or analysing repository code without editing it remains compatible with `none`' — but the Test Design's four offline rubric cases do not include a case exercising this read-only scenario, so the stated rule is untested by the plan's own test strategy.
findings.location: Approach / 'Criterion judgment and prompt discovery' vs. Test Design / 'Offline rubric behavior'
scenarios: An implementer writes a prompt that mis-classifies read-only code analysis as a file change; no test catches the regression.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Test Design 'Offline rubric behavior' list, add: '(5) a plan that reads or analyses repository source without editing any file produces PASS with no finding.'

evidence: Test Design: 'Also render a chunk containing both G5 and `no-file-impact` and assert both public context blocks reach the LLM request in stable order.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add documentation for the new `require_file_impact_scope` routing key (its semantics, accepted values, and interaction with other `applies_at` keys) to AGENTS.md or an equivalent criterion-author reference, and note this in the Scope section.
evidence: Plan says: 'Extend the shared routing validator in src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py to accept a non-empty list of non-empty strings for the new key' — but no corresponding doc update is listed in Scope.
The only new documentation artifact in Scope is `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md`, which documents the criterion for reviewers, not the routing-key contract for criterion authors.
ABSENCE: no AGENTS.md, schema-reference, or contributor-guide update appears in the Scope or Registration sections.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new `applies_at.require_file_impact_scope` routing-key contract that criterion authors must know about when writing future `criteria_routing.json` entries, but no plan section calls for updating AGENTS.md, a routing-schema reference, or any contributor-facing documentation to describe this new key and its semantics.
scenarios: A future contributor adding a criterion that should fire only for a specific file_impact_scope has no documented reference for the new routing key, risks using the wrong key name or format, and the validation error message may not be self-explanatory.

The architectural decision to extend `applies_at` with a value-list axis (distinct from the boolean `require_parent_id`) is not captured in any design doc, making it hard to reason about combinatorial routing behavior later.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief `applies_at` routing-key reference table to `AGENTS.md` (or the existing criterion-author guide) listing `require_parent_id` and the new `require_file_impact_scope` with their types and semantics. Reference this from the Scope section so implementers know to keep it current.

evidence: "render a chunk containing both G5 and no-file-impact and assert both public context blocks reach the LLM request in stable order" — only the dual-criterion case is called out
"Replace the single `extra` assignment with compositional `extra_parts`" — this changes existing G5 behavior
No test case for a G5-only chunk (no-file-impact absent) post-refactor is mentioned anywhere in Test Design or Acceptance Criteria
findings.finding: The plan refactors the pass1.py G5 inline branch into a compositional `extra_parts` list, but the specified test design only asserts the dual-criterion (G5 + no-file-impact) case. There is no specified test for a chunk containing G5 alone (without no-file-impact) to confirm the refactored path still delivers `decomp_context` correctly after the seam change.
scenarios: The compositional refactor incorrectly gates decomp_context on the presence of no-file-impact, breaking G5 context injection for tickets that have no file_impact_scope. The dual-criterion test passes but G5-only tickets silently lose their decomp_context.
findings.suggested_fix: In the prompt-input contract test block, add a third render case: a chunk with G5 criteria only (file_impact_scope absent or not 'none'). Assert `decomp_context` is present and the declared-reason block is absent. This directly guards the refactored G5-only branch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify at least one observability instrument (structured log line, metric counter, or trace span) for the no-file-impact LLM call at invocation, on LLM error/timeout, and on routing decision (selected vs. skipped) so operators can monitor cost and diagnose silent failures.
evidence: Plan says 'the existing advisory Pass-1 framework already owns LLM execution and fail-open behavior' but adds no logging/metric/alert specification for the new criterion path
ABSENCE: no mention of log.info/log.warning, metric increment, or trace annotation anywhere in the plan for this new LLM call
findings.finding: The plan adds a new gated LLM call for the no-file-impact criterion but specifies no observability instrumentation (log entry, metric counter, or trace span) for the new failure point — neither for successful invocation, LLM error, nor the routing decision that triggers it.
findings.location: Approach / Criterion judgment and prompt discovery; Approach / Deterministic applicability
scenarios: An operator notices unexpectedly high LLM spend but cannot distinguish no-file-impact calls from other Pass-1 calls
The routing predicate silently misfires (selecting or skipping the criterion incorrectly) with no log evidence to diagnose it
An LLM timeout on this criterion produces fail-open silence; support has no observable signal that the check was skipped
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief 'Observability' subsection to the Approach: emit a structured log at DEBUG on routing skip (`no-file-impact skipped: scope={scope}`), at INFO on invocation (`no-file-impact invoked: ticket={id}`), and at WARNING on LLM error before fail-open (`no-file-impact LLM error, failing open: {exc}`). This is consistent with the existing framework pattern and costs nothing at runtime on the common (non-none) path.
